patch:
diff --git a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
index 55fa844..732136e 100644
--- a/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
+++ b/evals/tasks/05-duplicate-orders/fixture/queries.py
@@ -1,11 +1,10 @@
-from store import CUSTOMERS, ORDERS
+from store import ORDERS
 
 
 def orders_for_customer(customer):
     """All orders belonging to `customer`."""
     rows = []
     for order in ORDERS:
-        owner = next(c for c in CUSTOMERS if c["id"] == order["customer_id"])
-        if owner["name"] == customer["name"]:
+        if order["customer_id"] == customer["id"]:
             rows.append(order)
     return rows
verification: 1) Reproduced the bug before fixing by printing the report: duplicates -- ('a@acme.test',101,50), ('a@acme.test',102,75), ('b@acme.test',101,50), ('b@acme.test',102,75), ('z@zenith.test',103,20), ('z@zenith.test',104,20); total_billed = 290. 2) After the fix: 4 correct lines, total_billed = 165, assertion every order_id appears at most once passed. 3) python3 run_tests.py printed 'visible tests passed'.
cause: queries.orders_for_customer joined ORDERS to CUSTOMERS on the non-unique name field. Two distinct customers share the name Acme, so every Acme order matched both Acme customers; orders 101/102 appeared twice, inflating total_billed from 165 to 290. Fix matches on the unique customer id.
